correctness.rationale: The proof reduces coverage exactly to an expectation of the strictly concave function \(h_z(q)=2\Phi(z\sqrt q)-1\) over a two-block weighted chi-square mean. The upper bound follows from pairwise coefficient averaging, which makes the uniform \(\nu\)-term mean minimal in convex order. The lower bound follows from the leave-one-out proof that \(\chi_k^2/k\) decreases in convex order with \(k\), stability of convex order under independent sums, and Jensen for a weighted average of iid copies. Equality and limiting cases are tracked explicitly. The numerical example is independently recomputed by verify.py.

originality.rationale: The exact Student-bridge law and its endpoint/balanced Student cases are prior and excluded from the novelty claim. The surviving claim is the sharp global ordering of the central coverage probability over every positive variance ratio, with explicit extremizers/infimum and a direct consequence for the prediction-powered mean interval. Targeted published-finding corpus searches, the own ledger, and the closest full-text primary literature did not reveal that statement or a stronger implication that contains it.
residual_risks: The Behrens--Fisher literature is extensive; an older paper not surfaced by the targeted searches could conceivably contain the same global central-coverage extremum even though the closest full-text bridge paper did not.
Richter 2020 supplies an exact fixed-parameter density, so the present contribution is a structural sharp optimization theorem over that family rather than a new distributional representation.

value.rationale: The source interval is a concrete prediction-powered mean interval whose displayed normal calibration is asymptotic in general. The theorem gives an exact finite-Gaussian best case, worst case, and variance-balance extremizer, showing quantitatively that the normal critical value undercovers even at its optimum for finite samples. This is a structural nuisance-parameter envelope rather than a routine one-parameter numerical evaluation.
